newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares rise 1.58 pct in selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares rise 1.58 pct in selective trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose in selective activity on Thursday as the market again tested resistance at the index's 1,670-1,680 range for the fourth day in a row, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,675, up 26 points, or 1.58 percent from Wednesday when it eased 0.6 percent in profit-taking. It moved beween 1,649-1,678 in the day.
Trade volume rose to 37.91 trillion lira ($266 million) from Wednesday's 33.14 trillion ($232.5 million), but included a 5.7 trillion lira ($40 million) block deal on the wholesale market.

The index had soared four percent on Monday and Tuesday, disregarding the possibility of early polls, after last week's 8.7 percent rally fuelled by hopes of an alternative alliance to replace the ailing Islamist-conservative coalition.
"Caution emerges when the index moves towards 1,700 mark and sales begin. But the general tendency is to buy," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti securities.
The 1,700 mark is the all-time high close set on January 27.

Brokers said negative effects of political uncertainty, including the possibility of snap polls to be held by end-1997 faded during the latest uptrend with the help of fresh liquidity inflow and skepticism over early elections.
"The index was squeezed at between 1,645 and 1,675 marks after several failures to break the 1,670-80 barrier," said Ibrahim Basnur from Ar securities.
"Putting aside the effects of political uncertainty, selling may increase in coming days if the index stays within this tight range and volume continues to drop," he added.
